# FileLoader

**Class:** `UltraCanvasFileLoader` · **Group:** [Application, windows and dialogs](../Groups/Application-Windows-And-Dialogs.md) · **Header:** [`UltraCanvas/include/UltraCanvasFileLoader.h`](../../../UltraCanvas/include/UltraCanvasFileLoader.h) · `#include "UltraCanvasFileLoader.h"`

## What it is for

Every file a user opens or saves: the dialogs, the readers and writers of every format, conversions, save settings.

The component documentation with explained, compiled C++ examples:

### enum `OfficeDocumentKind`

Which kind of office file a path is - what an office suite opens it as: a word-processing document (.odt, .docx, .doc, .md, .tex ...), a spreadsheet (.ods, .xlsx, .xls, .csv, .tsv), or a presentation (.pptx and kin, .odp and kin, .ppt and kin) - each with its templates (.ott, .dotx, .dotm; .ots, .xltx, .xltm; .potx, .potm, .otp, .pot). The extension decides; a file without a known one is looked into: an OpenDocument package by its mimetype entry, an Office Open XML package by its main part (word/, xl/, ppt/), a compound file holding a "PowerPoint Document" stream as a presentation. Unknown for anything else. Reads nothing beyond a ZIP's directory and its mimetype entry, or a compound file's directory.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `Unknown` |  |
| `Document` |  |
| `Spreadsheet` |  |
| `Presentation` |  |

### enum `TextExtractionMethod`

ExtractText takes as long as the file needs - recognition and transcription can take seconds - so call it off the UI thread (std::async) and show the result when it is done. It holds no lock while it reads, and both hooks are called on the thread that called ExtractText, so they must be callable from any thread.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `NoText` | no words to read in this type of file |
| `PlainText` | a text or code file, as it is |
| `Document` | a word processor document or a deck |
| `PDF` | the PDF's own text (recognition for a scanned one) |
| `Spreadsheet` | every sheet, tab-separated |
| `Recognition` | a picture: text recognition (OCR) |
| `Transcription` | a sound or a video: speech to text |
